pack.name: Brand Film — THE HANDOFF (60s)
pack.target_tools: Google Flow / Veo 3.1 Quality, 9:16, driven from the founder's own reference photographs via Flow's Ingredients / image-to-video mode for the three founder shots. Voiceover generated separately (Gemini-TTS / Google AI Studio) and synced in the edit — never baked into the Veo generation, which cannot hold one consistent voice across separate clips. Type is set in post if used at all; this film leans on voice, not text.
pack.logline: On the night someone new gets let in, we see what actually holds this group together — not the money, not the mask, the moment one of them chooses to open the door for someone else.
pack.pack_notes:
Eight shots, cut together on calm hard cuts, no whip pans, no speed ramps — same discipline as every other motion asset in this brand. Three shots (01, 03, 06) carry the founder's actual likeness and must be generated from his reference photographs, never from a text description of his appearance — see <founder_reference> below. The other five are ensemble or object shots under the standard "no identifiable face" rule, and per the updated casting doctrine, every ensemble shot is explicitly mixed-gender: Black men and women together, not men with women appearing only in a gathering shot.
VOICEOVER: seven lines, generated once as one continuous read in a single narrator voice, then cut to length per shot in the edit — do not generate line-by-line, since it is much harder to match tone and pacing across separate takes than to cut one clean read. Full script, read slowly, with real space between sentences:
"Time is money. We stopped spending ours. So we built the machine that prints it back. This is what we bought with it. Not the money — never the money. Just the ones who stopped keeping score. When one of us arrives, we all take it off. They chose sides. We chose each other."
CAR: written as an unbadged, low, matte-green Italian hybrid hypercar — scissor doors, wide low stance, quad exhaust. Never name the manufacturer or model in the prompt. The house doctrine already keeps every vehicle unbadged (see the racetrack teaser) — this is the same rule, and it reads as a Revuelto by silhouette without typing the word.
pack.founder_reference: Three source photographs, all supplied and approved by the founder for this purpose only: - TUX: a wedding photo, black tie, sharp daylight, 3/4 angle — primary reference for shots 03 and 06, since he is in black tie in both. - FRONT: a casual seated photo, clean even light, near-front angle — secondary reference for face structure, all three shots. - CLOSE: a direct close-up selfie, front-on — secondary reference for shot 01, which is the tightest, most intimate framing of the three. Use these as image-to-video start frames / character-reference ingredients. Do not generate his face from the text description alone — if a shot needs an angle none of the three references cover well, ask for another photo rather than approximating.

asset.title: Before
asset.vo_line: Time is money. We stopped spending ours.
asset.prompt: Vertical 9:16. A Black man alone in a dim private room just before dawn, dress shirt untucked and open at the collar, bow tie hanging loose and undone, jacket not yet on. Extreme close on his hands on a dark wood desk: a phone screen fading to black, a business card set face-down and left there, unread. Cut wide just enough to catch his reflection, soft and half-lit, in a dark window as grey pre-dawn light starts to show outside. He is still, unhurried, not performing for anyone. Camera holds in a slow, almost imperceptible push toward the hands, then the reflection. Cinematic digital cinema look, 40mm lens; T2.0, shallow depth of field, oval bokeh; single low practical light source, deep crushed blacks with retained shadow detail, subtle halation; desaturated near-monochrome palette of void black #050505, bone white #EDE7DC and aged gold #C8A96A; skin keyed a stop hotter than the room with soft fill on the shadow side, specular highlights rolling rather than clipping; heavy negative space, no eye contact with camera; fine organic film grain, print-film color science; quiet, private, unresolved. No on-screen text, no dialogue.

asset.title: Print Time
asset.vo_line: So we built the machine that prints it back.
asset.prompt: Vertical 9:16. Extreme macro, slow motion. A hand-operated gold foil press — old, heavy, hand-tooled brass and aged gold, not a modern machine — its stamp lowering in unhurried slow motion onto a dark metal plate. The instant of contact releases a soft pulse of warm gold light across the frame, like an ember catching, then fading back to a low glow that keeps breathing at the edges of the shot after the press lifts. No screens, no readouts, no numbers, no charts, no tickers, no dashboards, no UI of any kind — this is a purely mechanical, analog image standing in for "the machine." Fine dust catches the light on its way down. The frame above is empty black. Camera holds in one continuous slow push. Cinematic digital cinema look, 100mm macro lens; T2.0, extremely shallow depth of field, oval bokeh; deep crushed blacks, subtle halation on the gold; desaturated near-monochrome palette of void black #050505 and aged gold #C8A96A; abstract, patient, expensive. No on-screen text, no dialogue.

asset.title: Arrival
asset.prompt: Vertical 9:16. Night. A low, matte-green Italian hybrid hypercar glides to a stop on wet black tarmac outside an unmarked stone building — wide low stance, sharp angular body, quad exhaust, completely unbadged, no visible manufacturer marks or model text anywhere on the car. Its scissor door lifts open and up. A Black man in a full black-tie tuxedo steps out unhurried, an aged-gold Venetian half-mask held loose in one hand, not yet worn. One warm practical light from the building's doorway rakes across the wet ground and the car's paint, throwing a long specular line down its flank. Volumetric mist drifts low across the tarmac. The camera holds a slow lateral track alongside him as he crosses toward the light. asset.title: Into the Room
asset.vo_line: This is what we bought with it.
asset.prompt: Vertical 9:16. A tall arched doorway stands open in a black wall at the far end of a grand room, warm aged-gold light flooding out of it across a black marble floor thick with haze. Beyond the doorway, the room is full — Black men and women, evenly mixed throughout, in black tie and floor-length silk, mingling at ease, mid-conversation, backs and profiles to camera, nobody performing for the lens. A single figure in full black tie crosses the threshold from the dark into the light, moving steadily forward and only forward, mask now lowered in one hand. Slow embers drift up through the light. Camera holds a single continuous one-directional forward dolly-in toward the doorway for the full duration of the shot — the camera and the figure both move only forward, never pausing, never slowing to a stop, never reversing, never pulling back, never looping. The final frame must be closer to the doorway than the first frame. Cinematic digital cinema look, 40mm lens; T2.0, shallow depth of field, oval bokeh; single warm practical light source, deep crushed blacks with retained shadow detail, volumetric haze, subtle halation on highlights; skin keyed a stop hotter than the room with soft fill on the shadow side for every person in frame; desaturated near-monochrome palette of void black #050505, bone white #EDE7DC and aged gold #C8A96A; heavy negative space, level horizon, no eye contact with camera; fine organic film grain, print-film color science; ceremonial, warm, expensive. First ensemble shot in the film — set the mixed-gender room here clearly, since every later ensemble shot depends on it reading as an established, consistent crowd.
KNOWN FAILURE MODE (found 2026-08-09): the first generation of this shot exhibited a boomerang/reverse-motion artifact — the figure and camera moved forward into the doorway for roughly the first half of the clip, then the framing reversed back to something close to the opening composition by the final frame, i.e. it looks like he walked in and then walked back out. A person cannot un-walk through a doorway; this is a Veo continuity failure, not a valid take. It was caught by eye (scrubbing first/mid/last frame and comparing camera position) before ever reaching the repo. Fix applied above: explicit "only forward," "never reversing/pulling back/looping" language in the prompt, and reverse-motion terms added to the negative prompt. If a regeneration still shows this, the safest fix is to trim in Flow's editor to keep only the forward-moving portion of the clip (roughly the first half) rather than fighting the model for a full clean 8s.

asset.title: The Core
asset.vo_line: Not the money — never the money. Just the ones who stopped keeping score.
asset.prompt: Vertical 9:16. A single continuous slow lateral track through the gathering, passing small human moments in turn, none of them posed for camera: a Black woman laughing quietly with two others at a long candlelit table; a hand steadying a friend's shoulder in passing; someone catching a tipping glass before it falls and sliding it back without comment; two people, a man and a woman, sharing a private joke by a tall window with a soft skyline beyond. Warm candlelight and one low practical carry the room; haze drifts throughout. Every face stays in profile, three-quarter turn, or soft shadow — never toward the lens. The room is evenly mixed, Black men and women in black tie and floor-length silk throughout. Camera glides at a constant unhurried crawl, no shake, no cuts. Cinematic digital cinema look, 40mm lens; T2.0, shallow depth of field, oval bokeh; deep crushed blacks with retained shadow detail, volumetric haze, subtle halation; skin keyed a stop hotter than the room with soft fill on the shadow side for every person in frame; desaturated near-monochrome palette of void black #050505, bone white #EDE7DC and aged gold #C8A96A; heavy negative space, no eye contact with camera; fine organic film grain, print-film color science; intimate, warm, unhurried. asset.title: The Unmasking
asset.vo_line: When one of us arrives, we all take it off.
asset.prompt: Vertical 9:16. In the middle of the gathered room, a Black man in full black tie raises his aged-gold Venetian half-mask and removes it, unhurried, holding it at his side. He does not face the camera — three-quarter turn, profile toward the lens. A held beat of stillness follows. Then, around the room, others begin to do the same, one after another, not in unison, each at their own pace — Black men and women both, evenly mixed, each turning slightly toward one another rather than toward camera as they lower their masks, faces given to each other, not to the lens. Warm gold light holds steady through the room; haze drifts. Camera holds a slow, patient push into the center of the room across the whole beat, no cuts. Cinematic digital cinema look, 40mm lens; T2.0, shallow depth of field, oval bokeh; deep crushed blacks with retained shadow detail, volumetric haze, subtle halation; skin keyed a stop hotter than the room with soft fill on the shadow side for every person in frame; desaturated near-monochrome palette of void black #050505, bone white #EDE7DC and aged gold #C8A96A; heavy negative space, no eye contact with camera; fine organic film grain, print-film color science; ceremonial, warm, quietly emotional. No on-screen text, no dialogue.

asset.title: Close
asset.prompt: Vertical 9:16. Cut to total black. After a beat, the TEAM VILLAIN emblem fades up alone in the center of frame, aged gold on void black, softly lit as if by one distant practical, faint haze drifting past it. It holds, then begins a slow fade back to black. No other elements in frame. Shot in the same desaturated near-monochrome palette of void black #050505 and aged gold #C8A96A as the rest of the film; fine organic film grain. No on-screen text beyond the emblem itself, no dialogue.

asset.notes:
Pair this with the VLN-AUD-04 sub-drop stinger if generated, or reuse the tail of VLN-AUD-01. Silence for the last half-second reads better than music trailing off.
LOGO CONSISTENCY: the generated take renders Veo's own interpretation of the "TEAM VILLAIN" wordmark, not the real brand asset — it looks close but is not guaranteed pixel-consistent with assets/team-villain.png, and per house doctrine (xml/README.md, 04-emblem-motifs.xml) the emblem itself is never regenerated, only backplates for it. In the edit, use this clip as a backplate only: keep its black-to-glow lighting motion and haze, but composite the real team-villain.png (or team-villain-social.png) over it in place of the AI-rendered text, matched to the same fade-up/fade-out timing. Do not ship the AI-rendered wordmark as final.

pack.assembly_notes: Edit order is 01–08 in sequence, hard cuts, no transitions or crossfades except the final fade to black in 08. Total runtime target is 60s; if generated clip lengths don't land exactly on the beat marks above, trim from the tail of each clip rather than the head — every shot's strongest frame is near its end (the push has landed, the gesture has completed). Score: VLN-AUD-01 ducked under the voiceover throughout, with a sub-drop under the mask coming off in shot 06. Voiceover sits centered, ducked under score by roughly 6dB, silent gaps between lines left as written rather than compressed tight.
